idea-plugin.name: Commit Spotlight
idea-plugin.description:
See exactly what a commit touched, at a glance. Ever click through a commit in the Git Log and wonder exactly which lines it actually changed? Commit Spotlight highlights it for you — directly in your editor and across the commit's row in the Git Log — in a color you choose.

Highlight any commit's changes
Select one or more commits in the Git Log and highlight the lines they added, changed, or deleted, instantly, in any open editor.

Deletions you can actually see
There's no line left to highlight when something's deleted — so Commit Spotlight marks the spot with a colored divider and an inline label. Hover it to see exactly what was removed.

Color-code your investigation
Pick from 8 colors with adjustable opacity. Highlight different commits in different colors to visually separate what each one touched, and re-color any of them afterward without starting over.

Full-row highlighting in the Git Log
Highlighted commits are tinted across their entire row in the log, not just in the editor — so the color-coding works both ways.

Filter to just what matters
Flip on "Show Only Highlighted Commits" to collapse the Git Log down to exactly the commits you're tracking.

One click to open everything a commit touched
Jump straight to every file a commit changed, without hunting through the diff.

action.description: Highlight, in any open editor, the lines changed by the selected commit(s)
Remove commit-change highlights only for the currently selected commit(s)
Remove all commit-change highlights from every open editor

action.text: Show Only Highlighted Commits in Git Log
action.description: Filter the Git Log to show only currently highlighted commits

action.text: Prioritize Newest Commit on Overlapping Lines
action.description: Decides which commit wins when two highlighted commits touch the same line. Off (default): whichever commit you highlighted most recently wins, regardless of its actual commit date. On: whichever commit is chronologically newest wins, regardless of the order you highlighted them in.
Open every file touched by the currently selected commit(s)
